title: Bin El Ouidane reservoir on 21 Aug 2026
summary: On 21 Aug 2026 the radar shows a lake of 30.63 km2 inside the 10 km circle around Bin El Ouidane. No flag applies, and trees, shrub and rugged slopes cover 61.4% of the circle.

sections.heading: What the radar shows here
sections.text: Open water is the darkest type, at -18.04 dB in HH and -22.94 dB in HV, against a circle mean of -7.65 dB in HH and -14.36 dB in HV. The lake method finds 30.63 km2 of water.

sections.heading: Terrain types and what they mean
sections.text: Trees, shrub and rugged slopes give the brightest HV of the large types, -12.88 dB, because the pulse scatters around in leaves and branches. Rough dry ground and fields, 24.0% of the circle, sit at -10.57 dB in HH and -18.68 dB in HV. Built-up land, 1.8%, has an HV:HH ratio of -13.62 dB, the double-bounce signature of walls. Smooth bare ground, 2.8%, is almost as dark as the water in HV, at -21.35 dB.

sections.heading: Data quality notes
sections.text: No flag applies. The lake outline is approximate: 10.4% of it falls on land in the optical photo. Possible cause: radar shadow on steep shore slopes facing away from the single viewing direction. A shoreline survey would check it.
